dmitri: Heads up — product wants to move SIEM exports retention to 12 months for EU customers. Two quick asks: (1) how does this affect KMS key rotation/unwrapping (2) what RBAC changes do we need to gate access? cc @carla @mia
carla: For KMS: we can't rotate keys without ensuring old ciphertexts remain decryptable. We usually do a double-encrypt rotate with a 14-day overlap. Need to confirm exporters include key metadata so unwrapping can pick correct key.
mia: Agree on overlap. Also tagging: exported archives must be marked `sensitivity:security_logs` so downstream IAM can filter. That will map to a tighter access matrix.
ben: On RBAC, my proposal: only `sec-analyst`, `sec-oncall`, and `forensics` roles get read on exported buckets. Engineering product/metrics get aggregated alerts only. We can use JIT access for one-off investigations.
dmitri: Sounds good. Any runbook updates required? Also, does this change our audit logging scope for exports? Need to prove who requested data during incident triage.
security: Yes — add an audit entry at export generation + every object read. The exporter should emit events: `export.created`, `export.metadata.access_granted`, `export.object.read` with requester identity and justification. Store those events in the SIEM index and forward a subset to long-term archive.
carla: Example minimal RBAC policy (draft):
```json
{
  "resource": "projects/redwood/s3-exports/*",
  "bindings": [
    {"role": "roles/sec.analyst", "members": ["group:sec-analysts@redwood.com"]},
    {"role": "roles/sec.oncall", "members": ["serviceAccount:soc-oncall@redwood.com"]}
  ],
  "conditions": [{"title":"jit","expression":"request.time < timestamp_add(resource.metadata.requested_at, duration(7d))"}]
}
```
ben: +1 to that shape. For EU retention we also need export TTL tagging `ttl:365d` and a periodic job that enforces delete. Make sure deletion unwrapping handles KMS key rotation — i.e., we must not re-encrypt archival copies with a new key without retaining the old key material (or else we can't decrypt).
sre-bot: deploybot: Export pipeline 2026-03-21T15:02Z started; config-change=siem-export-retention-365d; author=ben
dmitri: On vuln triage / incident response: we should keep raw logs (full fidelity) for 90 days hot, then scrubbed indexed alerts for 12 months. Exports are separate — they're customer-facing/data-export artifacts and need stricter access and audit.
mia: One more compliance note: for GDPR, we need data minimization on exported payloads — strip user identifiers unless lit/forensics justification. Add a data-minimization toggle in exporter and require justification in the access request.
carla: I'll open a single ticket with checklist items: KMS rotation plan, RBAC matrix update, runbook updates, audit event schema, and deletion job. Linking in ticket and runbook drafts here: https://go.redwood.internal/issue/SEC-4389 and https://go.redwood.internal/runbooks/siem-export-handling
dmitri: Perfect. Can we have owners: KMS = infra-crypto (carla), RBAC + audit = security (mia + ben), runbook = dmitri. Target: draft changes by EOW and a staged rollout next sprint. :thumbsup:
security: noted, will prepare audit event schema and retention justification template.
ben: If anyone wants a quick review of the RBAC JSON, ping me and I'll do a pass.
carla: I'll include sample decrypt test in the runbook to validate rotated keys (script + sample objects).
dmitri: Thanks all — logging the action items in SEC-4389 now.
